description: Slack CLI - agent-first command line interface for Slack workspaces

auth.description: Slack token via SLACK_CLI_TOKEN_<PROFILE>, SLACK_CLI_TOKEN, or configured secret ref. Never store plaintext tokens in TOML or argv.

output.default: JSON envelope in non-TTY/agent mode, human-readable text in TTY
notes: set --output (or -o) to exactly one of auto, human, json, compact
auto picks human in a TTY and json otherwise
stdout carries one machine result on success or failure; human diagnostics use stderr
machine failures use the full {ok,meta,data,errors} envelope even in compact mode; stderr has no duplicate human error
paginated data includes pagination in json and compact; json keeps meta.pagination as a compatibility mirror
output_write_failed is io exit 8 and must not trigger replay of a mutation
agent-originated messages include attribution unless explicitly disabled
use command-local --blocks for raw Block Kit input
Markdown uses source-preserving Markdown fallback sections for unsupported block-level constructs
--blocks validates Slack Block Kit JSON rules before Slack mutation
Slack errors such as missing_scope, not_in_channel, and no_permission map to fixed exit codes

JSON results use {ok,meta,data,errors}; help and shell completion artifacts keep their raw text format. meta.exit_code is present on success and failure. Discovery schema is data.schema; guides are data.document. Compact success is bare data.

cache.clear: no resource clears all cache files for the profile
file.upload: --blocks Block Kit JSON array for --message comment
health.api-test: calls unauthenticated Slack Web API api.test
health.check: runs api.test plus Slack Status current
data.healthy is true when api_ok is true and there are no active incidents for the requested scope
health.current: calls unauthenticated slack-status.com v2 current endpoint
health.history: --limit <n> defaults to 20; 0 returns all fetched incidents
calls unauthenticated slack-status.com v2 history endpoint
message.scheduled.list: data.scheduled_messages[] rows include id/channel/post_at/text_preview plus best-effort channel_name/channel_hr/channel_url/channel_type/channel_user/is_dm metadata
message.send: source-preserving Markdown fallback for unsupported block-level constructs
--blocks validates Slack Block Kit JSON rules
--schedule <RFC3339|duration|unix-seconds> for channel or user scheduled sends
scheduled --user sends resolve/open the DM before chat.scheduleMessage; real output data.channel is the raw DM/MPIM channel ID

compact: command-specific data on success, including pagination for paginated operations
health.api-test: data.args when Slack echoes request arguments
human: Slack channels, DMs, and permalinks may be OSC 8 terminal hyperlinks; do not parse human output
message.scheduled.list: data.scheduled_messages[].channel raw ID for delete targets
human table columns ID/CHANNEL/DM/POST_AT/TEXT; human CHANNEL may be a friendly #channel or @user label
output_flag: --output (or -o) selects one of auto, human, json, compact
auto picks human in a TTY and json otherwise

auth: printf '%s\n' "$SLACK_TOKEN" | slick auth login --workspace default --method token --token-stdin
slick auth login --workspace default --method token --token-env SLACK_CLI_TOKEN_DEFAULT
file: tar czf - build/ | slick file upload --channel C123 --file - --filename build.tgz
manifest: slick manifest template --name example --format json --output=human > manifest.json
slick manifest template --name example --format yaml --output=human > manifest.yaml
message: slick message send --user dev@example.com,ops@example.com --message 'PR is ready'
slick message scheduled delete --channel C123 --scheduled-id Q123 --dry-run

best_practices: Prefer channel/user IDs over display names in automation.
Use --blocks when message-like input is already Slack Block Kit JSON.
Use --dry-run before destructive or high-visibility mutations.
Use --output=compact when another tool expects command-specific JSON only.
Follow meta.pagination.next_cursor while meta.pagination.has_more is true.
Prime users and channels with cache commands before repeated lookup or completion-heavy work.
Load the workflow runbook with slick agent guide <workflow> before operating.
anti_patterns: Do not store Slack tokens in TOML or source files.
Do not pass raw Slack tokens in argv.
Do not use --output to select raw Block Kit input; use command-local --blocks for that.
Do not disable agent attribution unless explicitly required.
Do not parse human-readable output in scripts; use JSON.
Do not assume one search page means there are no more matches.
Do not duplicate attribution text in the message body.
